blocks.title: Standard enthalpy change of neutralization
blocks.text: The standard enthalpy change of neutralization, delta Hn, is the enthalpy change when one mole of water is formed by the reaction of an acid with an alkali under standard conditions. It is always exothermic.

The enthalpy of neutralization of NaOH by HCl is -57.1 kJ per mol. When the solutions are mixed the only change is the formation of water molecules, leaving Na+ and Cl- as free ions in solution; so the enthalpy of neutralization is merely the heat of formation of one mole of liquid water from its ions, H+(aq) + OH-(aq) gives H2O(l), delta Hn = -57.1 kJ per mol. For all strong acid-strong base reactions delta Hn is always near -57.1 kJ per mol.
